executions.rationale: The WAL archiver is a long-lived server execution with an upstream main function.
The autovacuum launcher is a long-lived server execution.
Each autovacuum worker is launched as an independent backend execution.
A normal client connection uses one backend execution thread in threaded runtime.
Background workers include extension workers and short-lived parallel workers.
The background writer is a long-lived server execution.
The checkpointer is a long-lived server execution.
Upstream declares no launchable main function; a request must fail closed until a dedicated adapter exists.
Upstream declares no launchable main function; a request must fail closed until a dedicated adapter exists.
Connection rejection and early startup failures still require isolated backend execution.
The invalid sentinel is not a launchable backend execution.
Each PostgreSQL asynchronous I/O worker requires an independent execution.
The logging collector requires explicit descriptor ownership and shutdown in one process.
The replication slot synchronization worker has an upstream main function.
Standalone mode is the supervisor execution itself and is never launched as a child.
Startup and recovery run in a dedicated backend execution.
The WAL receiver is a long-lived replication execution.
A WAL sender starts as B_BACKEND and changes its logical type after authentication.
The WAL summarizer is a long-lived server execution.
The WAL writer is a long-lived server execution.
